verdict.rationale: The reflect.app page claims local Markdown files with sync via iCloud Drive or Git, which would let users own and read notes without the app. Other first-party docs describe a server-backed model instead: notes stored encrypted on Reflect's servers, API access, and export to HTML/Markdown. Nothing addresses offline operation, so ownership is only thinly and inconsistently evidenced. Missing for 10: any documentation that the app works fully offline, consistent first-party detail on the local file storage format and location, and independent or hands-on confirmation that notes are readable without the app.

support.subject: As a power-user, my notes live in local files or a local-first store that I own and can read without the app, and everything keeps working fully offline

citations.quote: An open-source note-taking app with daily notes, backlinks, and local Markdown files.
Your choice of sync. Use iCloud Drive or Git.
you can always export it into an open format (like HTML or Markdown).
